title: docs(guide): author `object-grid` filter in the canonical array form
body:
Fixes #7713

`content/docs/guide/objectos-integration.mdx` authored `object-grid.filter` as an `and:`-keyed object of `{ field, operator, value }` entries. It now authors the registry's canonical array, the two entries AND-ed implicitly, and the comment above the key says what the key actually is.

```diff
-  // ObjectQL filter syntax
-  filter: {
-    and: [
-      { field: 'status', operator: 'eq', value: 'active' },
-      { field: 'created_date', operator: 'gte', value: '2024-01-01' }
-    ]
-  },
+  // Grid filter, JSON-rules form: an array of `{ field, operator, value }`
+  // entries, AND-ed together. `operator` takes the canonical view-filter
+  // vocabulary (`equals`, `greater_than_or_equal`, ...).
+  filter: [
+    { field: 'status', operator: 'equals', value: 'active' },
+    { field: 'created_date', operator: 'greater_than_or_equal', value: '2024-01-01' }
+  ],
```

One file, 7 insertions, 7 deletions. No `packages/**` change: adding an `and` / `$and` branch to `convertFiltersToAST` is objectui#6948's card, not this one.

## The declared type of `filter`, and why the gate was green on the wrong shape

Measured on this branch:

- **Registry** — `packages/plugin-grid/src/index.tsx:218` registers `{ name: 'filter', type: 'array', ... 'Filter criteria in JSON-rules form. The canonical spelling ...' }`.
- **Declared type** — `packages/types/src/objectql.ts:679`, on `ObjectGridSchema`: `filter?: any[];` (doc comment: "Array-based filter configuration"). The array form is the DECLARED form, not only the registry's.
- **Prior art in the tree** — `packages/plugin-grid/README.md:468` and `:529` already show the array form, both under `const schema: ObjectGridSchema = { ... }`.

`check:doc-snippets` was green on the object form for one reason, and it is not coverage: **the example's literal is a bare `const schema = { ... }` with no type annotation**, so `ObjectGridSchema.filter?: any[]` was never consulted. Two controls, both run on this tree and both restored byte-identically:

1. **The block IS compiled.** Injecting `dataSource: zzzUndefinedIdent,` at `:278` turned the gate RED — `content/docs/guide/objectos-integration.mdx:278:15  TS2304: Cannot find name 'zzzUndefinedIdent'.` / `Semantic phase: 477 of 477 block(s) judged, 1 failed.` Green was never "not covered".
2. **The annotation would have caught it.** Adding `import type { ObjectGridSchema } from '@object-ui/types';` and annotating the literal, with the pre-fix `and:` object still in place, turned the gate RED with exactly one diagnostic: `content/docs/guide/objectos-integration.mdx:282:5  TS2353: Object literal may only specify known properties, and 'and' does not exist in type 'any[]'.`

Control 2 is not applied here — annotating the literal is outside this card's scope fence (the fence is the `filter` value and the comment above it). It is filed as **objectui#7972**, same class as objectui#7778.

## Operator vocabulary: `eq` / `gte` were deprecated aliases, not members

The card's prescription named only the array shape, so the operator spelling was measured separately, against the shipped `@objectstack/spec`:

```
VIEW_FILTER_OPERATORS = ["equals","not_equals","contains","not_contains","icontains",
  "starts_with","ends_with","greater_than","less_than","greater_than_or_equal",
  "less_than_or_equal","in","not_in","is_empty","is_not_empty","is_null","is_not_null",
  "before","after","between"]

normalizeFilterOperator('eq')  === 'equals'
normalizeFilterOperator('gte') === 'greater_than_or_equal'
```

Neither `eq` nor `gte` is a member; both live only in `VIEW_FILTER_OPERATOR_ALIASES`, whose own doc comment reads: *"Deprecated: new producers MUST emit the canonical forms; these aliases are a migration bridge and may be dropped in a future major."* `packages/plugin-grid/README.md` — the tree's own authority for this key — already spells the canonical `equals` / `after`.

The lowering is byte-identical either way (`viewFilterRuleToNode` normalises first), so this changes nothing at runtime. Along the four decision axes: **real need** — a doc example is a producer, and every copy of it emits the deprecated spelling; **long-term** — contract-first, one vocabulary rather than N dialects, which is the alias table's own stated purpose; **AI-error prevention** — teaching the alias is exactly the tolerance-hides-mistakes shape, since the fold is silent and the author never learns the canonical name; **startup focus, no gradualism** — the maintainer's 2026-08-27 ruling retires deprecated spellings immediately rather than in stages, and there is no named external user of the alias in the docs. All four point the same way, so there is no trade-off to hand up.

## Ablation, reported as observed (no red/green pin is owed here)

On the committed tree, the `and:`-keyed object was put back — the mutated file hashed to `3115b38eafb92ccf8ba1ba15b138668a61eea3f8`, which is `origin/main`'s own blob for this page, so the mutation provably reproduced the pre-fix bytes exactly. With it in place:

```
ABLATION check:doc-snippets EXIT=0
Semantic phase: 477 of 477 block(s) judged, 0 failed.
Every covered documentation snippet compiles against the built types.
ABLATION check:doc-types EXIT=0  ✅  Every documented component type is registered.
```

**The gate stays GREEN on the defect.** That is the finding's point: no reader in this repository refuses this shape. Restore leg: `git checkout HEAD -- ...`, blob back to `1db05a62866e59329427841aaf020f10da81ad6d`, `git diff HEAD` empty. Marker observation on disk: the canonical-array marker counted 1 before the mutation, 0 after it, 1 after the restore.

This PR owes no new red/green pin. The docs-only fix has no runtime face, and the mechanism gap (`convertFiltersToAST` has no `and` branch) is objectui#6948's card. What this PR can honestly claim is that the page no longer teaches a shape no reader lowers; it cannot claim anything now stops the shape coming back — objectui#7972 is that repair.

## Out of scope, filed unassigned

- **objectui#7971** — `content/docs/fields/lookup.mdx:43` and `content/docs/fields/user.mdx:43` author `lookupFilters` with the same deprecated aliases (`eq`, `ne`). Different pages, different key: not touched here.
- **objectui#7972** — the bare-literal / no-annotation hole described above; 24 unannotated `const schema = {` literals across 12 doc pages, against 20 annotated across 9.

Measured and deliberately left alone: `and: [` occurs exactly once under `content/docs` on `origin/main` — the instance this PR fixes. The `// ObjectQL sorting` comment two lines below is untouched (it describes `sort`, outside the fence), and `$filter: { status: 'active' }` at `:306` is a MongoDB-style record, which IS one of the three shapes `toFilterNode` lowers.
